CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Rachel is a 48-year-old female presenting with shortness of breath that occurs with mild exercise or walking. She reports palpitations accompanying the dyspnea, such as when walking up her driveway. She notes the symptoms have been occurring more frequently lately. She is uncertain if the back pain contributes to or triggers these episodes. Patient reports recent increase in exercise activity to address weight gain. She denies other recent lifestyle changes or new allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies other issues bothering her at this time. Mild wheezes noted on lung examination.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Chronic back pain
Smoking history

MEDICATIONS
Effexor for depression
Gabapentin (Neurontin) for chronic back pain

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a smoker, currently smoking approximately one cigarette per day, down from two packs per day at last visit. Patient reports recent increase in exercise activity. Patient has considered doing yoga but has not made it a regular habit.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears well.
Lungs: Mild wheezes noted throughout all lung fields bilaterally. Diaphragm appears slightly flattened on imaging.
Otherwise: Normal physical examination.

RESULTS
Pulmonary Function Tests: Results suggest possible asthma or COPD.
Chest X-ray: Flattened diaphragm consistent with COPD, commonly seen in smokers.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): Newly diagnosed. Patient started on Combivent inhaler, two puffs twice daily to help open airways. Albuterol prescribed as rescue inhaler for acute shortness of breath. Prednisone taper prescribed. Patient advised to continue smoking cessation efforts.
Depression: Stable on current Effexor regimen. Continue current medication. Encouraged to engage in yoga for depression and back pain management.
Chronic Back Pain: Continue Gabapentin (Neurontin). Continue rest as needed when pain is severe. Encouraged to incorporate yoga into routine.
